title: Finding Piecewise Formulas for Parametric Ramp and Square-Wave Signals
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a piecewise formula in terms of the positive constants T and A for each graphed signal: (a) a ramp signal on [0, T] that equals 0 on [0, T/2] and rises linearly from (T/2, 0) to (T, 1); (b) a square wave on [0, 2T] that alternates between +A on [0, T/2) and [T, 3T/2) and -A on [T/2, T) and [3T/2, 2T].
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & 0 \le x \le T/2 \\ \frac{2}{T}x - 1, & T/2 < x \le T \end{cases}; \quad \text{(b) } f(t) = \begin{cases} A, & 0 \le t < T/2 \text{ or } T \le t < 3T/2 \\ -A, & T/2 \le t < T \text{ or } 3T/2 \le t \le 2T \end{cases}

steps.title: Find the Ramp Equation for Signal (a)
steps.explanation: On [0, T/2], the graph lies on the x-axis, so f(x) = 0. On (T/2, T], the segment joins (T/2, 0) to (T, 1) with slope 2/T, giving f(x) = (2/T)x - 1.
steps.why: Using point-slope form at the x-intercept (T/2, 0) immediately yields y = (2/T)(x - T/2) = (2/T)x - 1.

steps.title: Identify the Alternating Constant Branches for Signal (b)
steps.mathExpression: f(t) = \begin{cases} A, & 0 \le t < \frac{T}{2} \\ -A, & \frac{T}{2} \le t < T \\ A, & T \le t < \frac{3T}{2} \\ -A, & \frac{3T}{2} \le t \le 2T \end{cases}
steps.explanation: The square wave switches between +A and -A every half-period T/2, with solid dots on the left of each half-period step and open circles on the right (and a solid dot at the final endpoint t = 2T).
steps.why: A periodic square wave of period T and amplitude A takes constant values +A and -A on alternating half-periods of length T/2.

steps.title: Verify Continuity and Boundary Values
steps.explanation: Checking the ramp formula at x = T/2 and x = T confirms that it matches the endpoints (T/2, 0) and (T, 1) in graph (a).
steps.why: Evaluating the linear formula at both endpoints verifies algebraic consistency with the geometric figure.
